title: Living ashtpadi 23
hook: clear sight is a gift, not a skill

segments.voice: Yesterday, drisat, and your line: lit by the One. Did you catch yourself looking, three times? Today we carry the whole twenty-third ashtpadi, the cleared eyes, out into the day. Day five hundred twenty-nine.

The first week in a new apartment, you notice everything. The way the light hits the kitchen at four o'clock. The creak in the third stair. The neighbor's wind chime. A year later, you walk past all of it without a glance. Nothing changed. The light still comes in at four. You just stopped seeing it. That fading is ordinary, and easy to miss. The twenty-third ashtpadi has something to say about it, from an unexpected direction.
screen: `THE FIRST WEEK: YOU NOTICE EVERYTHING.` → `A YEAR LATER: NOTHING.` → `AN UNEXPECTED ANSWER.`

segments.voice: Here's the twenty-third ashtpadi in brief. The Guru applies giaan anjan, the eye-ointment of wisdom, and the darkness of not-knowing ends. With cleared eyes, God is seen within and without. And God is found at both ends of every look, the seer and the seen. Now, the natural modern response to all that would be: great, how do I train my eyes? What's the technique? Sukhmani gently sets that aside. Look again at the salok. Who gave the ointment? The Guru. How did the seeker meet the holy one? Har kirpaa te: by God's grace. Clear sight, in this ashtpadi, isn't a skill you master like a language or a golf swing. It's a gift you receive. That doesn't make practice pointless. Sikh practice still includes amrit vela, the company of the sangat, recitation. One way to picture it: practice is more like opening the shutters than building a lamp. In the salok's picture, the light comes from elsewhere. You can make room for it; you can't manufacture it. And there's real freedom in that. If seeing freshly were a skill, every dull, blurry day would be your failure. If it's a gift, then a blurry day is just a day the shutters stuck, and tomorrow the light may come in again. The last word of the salok is pargaas, the mind lit up. Not lit by effort; lit, the way a room is lit when the sun comes through.
screen: `THE ASHTPADI: OINTMENT, SIGHT, SEER.` · `HAR KIRPAA TE: BY GOD'S GRACE.` · `OPENING SHUTTERS, NOT BUILDING LAMPS.` · `A BLURRY DAY IS NOT A FAILURE.` · then, large: `SEE FRESHLY.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: pause and see freshly. Choose something you see every day and never notice: a doorframe, a mug, the view from your usual chair. Look at it as if you'd just moved in. Its color, its shape, a scratch, the way light lands on it. Don't force a feeling. Just leave the shutters open and see what comes in. If nothing does, that's fine too. If you pray, you can say Waheguru as you look. The bell holds the time.
Pargaas, light or illumination: clear sight comes by grace, har kirpaa te; practice opens the shutters, and pargaas comes in.
Your line: see freshly. Today, on your most familiar route, look up once and find one thing you've never noticed before. Day five hundred twenty-nine.

screen: `DAY 529 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: ASHTPADI 24, SALOK: THE PERFECT LORD.`

howItsDone: Sikhs reciting Sukhmani Sahib's twenty-third ashtpadi hear that clear sight comes by God's grace and the Guru's wisdom, and they keep daily practice as a way of making room for that light.

fork.setup: it's a dull day, and nothing looks fresh. by the twenty-third ashtpadi, what is this?
options: a day the shutters stuck; the light may come tomorrow.
a sign to give up practice.
fork.reveal: clear sight is a gift, not a skill, so a blurry day isn't your failure. you keep the shutters open, and the light comes by grace.

original.note: Gurmukhi: pargaas, light or illumination; the salok's last word, the mind lit up.

trapdoor: what you thought: seeing freshly is a mindfulness skill.
what it means: in Sukhmani, clear sight is a gift of grace; practice makes room for it.
what a scholar hears: the salok credits the ointment to the Guru, gur deeaa, and the meeting to God's grace, har kirpaa te, leaving the seeker no technique to claim.
